 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2- Sangavva W/O Gadigeppa Baradeli vs The Assistant Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58084083/
1  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11429  MFA No. 102051 of 2016
ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 29th September 2015 passed in MVC No.2549/2013 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & Addl. MACT, Ramdurg at Ramdurg1.
2.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & Addl. MACT, Ramdurg at Ramdurg1
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that, on 15.04.2013 at about 4:30 p.m., when the deceased was proceeding on the left side of the road at Ter Bazar of Ramdurg, the driver of the Mahindra Bolero Vehicle bearing registration No.KA-24/G-42 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner, in high speed, dashed to the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries to his head and other parts of his body.

Immediately, he was shifted to the Government Hospital at Ramdurg and thereafter to the SDM Hospital at Dharwad,
wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 16.04.2013 to 07.05.2013.
On 07.05.2013 at SDM Hospital at Dharwad 'Tribunal', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11429 the deceased was succumbed to the said injuries.
Hence, the petitioner - wife of the deceased filed claim petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation.
3. The respondent Nos.1 & 2 entered appearance and filed objection statement denying the averments made in the claim petition and sought dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The claimant examined herself as PW1 and got marked 14 documents as per Exs.P1 to P14.
On behalf of the respondents, two witnesses were examined as RW1 & RW2 and produced 4 documents as per Exs.R1 to R4.

The Tribunal on appreciation of the entire material available on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,85,921/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization of the entire amount.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant is in appeal seeking higher compensation.

5. Learned counsel Shri H.M. Dharigond appearing for the appellant-claimant submits that the Tribunal has NC: 2024:KHC-D:11429 committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month as the deceased was working as Agricultural Coolie.

Further, he submits that the Tribunal has not appreciated the pleadings and evidence in a proper perspective and awarded meager compensation of Rs.40,000/- on all other conventional heads, for the accidental death,
which is contrary to the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.Pranay Sethi & Others2.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs.Pranay Sethi & Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, she seeks to enhance the same appropriately by allowing the appeal.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP appearing for the respondents oppose the appeal and submits that the appellant has failed to prove the income of the deceased before the Tribunal and hence, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month, which does not call for any Sangavva W/O Gadigeppa Baradeli vs The Assistant Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58084083/
2 modification.

entities.text: Sangavva W/O Gadigeppa Baradeli vs The Assistant Director
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of appeal papers, the only point that would arise for consideration in this appeal is as to, whether the appellant is entitled for higher compensation?
8.

It is not in dispute that in a road traffic accident occurred on 15.04.2013, the deceased-Gadigeppa,
husband of the appellant, succumbed to the injuries.
The Tribunal, while determining the compensation has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month.
Though the claimant pleaded that the deceased was an agricultural coolie and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
However, no cogent and legally acceptable evidence was placed on record by the claimants to substantiate the income of the deceased.
In the absence of any cogent evidence to prove the income of the deceased, it is for the Courts to assess the monthly income notionally, taking note of the income chart prepared by the KSLSA.
As per the chart, the notional income for the year 2014 is Rs.7,000/- per month.
Hence, NC: 2024:KHC-D:11429 taking note of the same, this Court reassesses notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month.
In terms of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi supra, the deceased was aged 62 years as on the date of accident, the appropriate multiplier would be 7.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation3, as there is one dependent, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased is to be taken at 50% of the assessed income.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation under the head of "loss of dependency" at Rs.2,94,000/- (Rs.7,000-50%x12x7).
9.

Further, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses and transportation of dead body with 10% escalation.

In terms of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram & Others4, the appellant- claimant would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of consortium' with 10% escalation.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram & Others4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, the compensation of Rs.93,921/-
awarded under the head medical expenses is retained.

11. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to modified compensation on the following heads:
Loss of dependency Rs.2,94,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.16,500/-
 Funeral expenses  & transportation of dead body Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of consortium Rs.44,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs.93,921/-
Sangavva W/O Gadigeppa Baradeli vs The Assistant Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58084083/
3  ------------------
 Total Rs.4,64,921/-
 ------------------
12.

In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
2018 ACJ 2782 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11429 ORDER (i) Appeal stands partly allowed.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the  Tribunal is modified holding that the  claimants are entitled to total  compensation of Rs.4,64,921/- as against Rs.3,85,921/- awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
(iv) The respondents shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11429 (v) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made in terms of award of the Tribunal.
(vi) Registry to draw modified award accordingly.
(vii) No costs.

Sd/-
(VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL) JUDGE VNP, CT:VP Sangavva W/O Gadigeppa Baradeli vs The Assistant Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58084083/
